notes: Both evaluate LOH events and drug resistance association (C5, C40, C62-C65, C141). LLM finds evidence sufficient with multiple lines of support. Peer reviewers acknowledge the observations but require statistical modeling to assess significance of LOH-MIC coincidences, stating 'without proper statistics it is not possible to evaluate' whether patterns are selective or chance.

Both agree on aneuploidy findings (C7, C43-C45, C68, C70-C71, C144): prevalent but transient, not consistently correlated with MIC. Peer reviewers do not challenge these descriptive observations, implicitly accepting them as adequately supported.

Both rate deletion mutant validation (C116-C119) as UNCERTAIN. LLM notes limited validation (only 1/23 genes affecting MIC) but views fitness effects positively. Peer reviewers express dissatisfaction with scope and conclusiveness, stating validation 'was not as conclusive as one would like regarding the MIC phenotype.'

Both accept phenotypic variation findings (C98-C102, C153) regarding adhesion, filamentation, and virulence. Peer reviewers acknowledge 'a degree of phenotypic assessment' and state methodologies are 'state of the art,' with no specific concerns raised about these measurements.

Major disagreement on genetic diversity interpretation (C56-C60, C124). LLM views substantial within-patient diversity as supporting diverse genotype populations. Peer reviewers fundamentally challenge this, arguing variants are pre-existing standing variation, not arising during treatment, citing implausible mutation rates and same-day isolates differing by thousands of SNPs.

Both evaluate 240 recurrently mutated genes (C41-C42, C76). LLM finds statistical significance (p < 10⁻⁴) sufficient. Peer reviewers acknowledge the finding but state 'very little statistical modeling to assess how likely these combinations...are due to real selective events...or just by chance' and 'it is hard to know which signals are truly significant.'

Partial overlap on sequencing methodology (C51-C52). LLM rates study design and SNP calling as SUPPORTED (93.9% concordance). Peer reviewers express serious concern about SNP calling accuracy (87.3% average, <65% in half of series), calling this 'worrying' and an 'important limitation,' undermining confidence in mutation calls.

Minimal overlap (C124 only). LLM R15 addresses C. albicans vs C. glabrata diversity comparison as SUPPORTED. Peer R5 challenges the fundamental premise that variants arose during treatment (standing variation argument), which undermines the evolutionary comparison framework.

LLM evaluates aneuploidy-LOH mechanism hypothesis (C72-C73, C110, C145-C147) as UNCERTAIN, noting plausible but speculative mechanism. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific claims.

LLM evaluates driver mutations in 17 genes (C66-C67, C78-C80, C89-C90) as SUPPORTED, particularly ERG11 involvement. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific driver mutation claims.

LLM evaluates functional enrichment of cell wall/surface genes (C81-C88, C91, C149) as SUPPORTED with significant p-values. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific enrichment claims.
LLM evaluates NMF clustering and co-occurrence patterns (C92-C97) as SUPPORTED with strong statistical significance. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these clustering claims.
LLM evaluates fitness cost and compensatory evolution patterns (C104-C109) as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific fitness trajectory claims.
LLM evaluates Patient 1 aneuploidy as transient intermediate example (C111-C115) as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this specific case study.
LLM evaluates genotype-phenotype correlation for filamentation (C154-C155) as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this specific example.
